claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A domain-adapted transformer can fuse minimal ab initio descriptors with experimental microstructural characterizations of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed fused model can accurately predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
Brief ab initio calculations can provide sufficient descriptors of local bonding environments and electronic structure for the proposed model.
Experimentally measured microstructural features can adequately capture the hierarchical heterostructure and its multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Fusion of physics-based descriptors and experimental data maps the hierarchical structure onto macroscopic mechanical behavior.
The transformer's attention mechanism captures long-range, multiscale interactions between atomic-scale descriptors and global microstructural features.
Capturing these multiscale interactions enables representation of cracking mechanisms and elastic–plastic responses.
Representing cracking and elastic–plastic responses improves prediction accuracy for tensile and fracture properties.
The proposed model will be approximately 5–10 times more efficient than full ab initio or extensive CALPHAD computations.
The proposed model will reduce prediction errors, including fracture-toughness RMSE, by roughly 20–30% relative to existing methods.
Detailed ab initio, CALPHAD, and traditional machine-learning methods are computationally intensive.
Existing methods are less accurate at predicting fracture toughness than the proposed approach.
The approach may lose reliability when its training data do not represent the range of microstructural heterogeneities in HfNbTiVAl10.
The approach may lose reliability at very high strain rates or non-ambient temperatures outside the training domain.
The magnitude of the model's accuracy and efficiency gains depends on the quality and variability of the integrated physics and experimental data.

contradictions.description: The stated application domain includes unspecified service temperatures, while the boundary states that non-ambient temperatures may be outside the reliable domain. Because service temperatures can be non-ambient, the intended valid temperature range is internally ambiguous.
